採用・広告の製品.quote: Andromeda’s spatial navigation system provides surgeons with GPS-like guidance through human anatomy, ensuring they always know where they are and what to do next. With a iPad interface, learning new procedures becomes streamlined. Surgeons can master techniques without a burdensome robotic training program.

We are developing proprietary AI models that will allow for surgeon-in-the-loop autonomous surgical tasks. Our software will act as a "sous surgeon", leveraging data from thousands of cases to supercharge surgical decisions.
Our goal: Enable surgeons to perform more procedures per day and empower every surgeon to deliver optimal results to every patient, every time.
Andromeda's software platform continuously improves. Regular updates mean new capabilities, enhanced precision, and expanded procedures.

Our open architecture seamlessly integrates with existing surgical tools, allowing any interventional procedure to run on our platform. It's not just a surgical robot. It's the brain at the center of the operating room of the future.
Founded by Serial Autonomy & Healthcare Entrepreneurs

Nick Damiano (CEO) and Kartik Tiwari (CTO) launched Andromeda Surgical in San Francisco, combining deep medtech experience with autonomous vehicle expertise. Nick previously founded two successful medtech companies (Zenflow and Avail MedSystems), while Kartik co-founded Starsky Robotics and built the world's first driverless truck on public roads.
World's First Robotic-Assisted HoLEP Procedure

Achieved a historic medical milestone with the world's first robotic-assisted HoLEP (RoLEP™) procedure performed at Universidad Católica in Santiago, Chile. Dr. Cristián Trucco completed the surgery using their tablet-based interface, launching the ASTRA clinical trial under the leadership of Prof. Peter Gilling, who pioneered the HoLEP procedure in 1997.

With successful clinical trials ongoing in various countries, Andromeda Surgical is preparing to scale beyond HoLEP procedures into additional surgical specialties. Our long-term vision positions us as "the Tesla of Surgical Robotics"—enabling every surgeon to operate at world expert level through progressive autonomy and AI assistance.
Serial healthcare founder who has built hardware and software products that have launched in 1,000 hospitals.

The product is only available for sale in Canada and New Zealand. We are designing this product with the intent to improve surgery. All information on this website represents design goals and should not be construed as claims.

Andromeda Surgical is developing AI-powered robotic systems to democratize complex surgical procedures, starting with HoLEP for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Their technology combines AI guidance with off-the-shelf robotic arms to improve surgical outcomes and efficiency while reducing the steep learning curve for surgeons.
Your Privacy on this Website

Phaze Ventures first invested in Andromeda at seed in September 2025, when the company had performed the world's first robotic-assisted HoLEP procedure in Santiago, Chile, and not much else. Nine months later, Standard Capital led the Series A.

Andromeda now holds regulatory clearance in Canada and New Zealand, with further approvals in progress, and expects its first commercial systems in hospitals within two months. More news on the launch is coming soon.
Phaze Ventures is proud to continue backing Nick, Kartik, and the Andromeda team as they move into commercial launch. The best is yet to come.

Andromeda Surgical builds autonomous surgical robots designed to make surgery safer, easier, and more efficient. The company's first indication is HoLEP, with a broader vision to build an AI-guided platform for multiple surgical procedures.

HoLEP has been the gold-standard treatment for enlarged prostate since 1998 but has seen limited adoption precisely because it requires extensive training to master.[2] By reducing this learning curve, Andromeda unlocks a massive addressable market—most urologists currently cannot perform the procedure at expert level, creating artificial scarcity in access to optimal outcomes.

Building a functional robotic platform in three months is exceptional in an industry where hardware development typically spans years.[1] This speed reflects both the founders' autonomous vehicle background (where rapid iteration is standard) and their deliberate choice to avoid mechanical complexity by targeting natural orifice procedures.
